summary: This is a fiction excerpt from a numbered book section in which Rebecca brings the Simpson baby home for a Sunday visit, but Miss Miranda refuses to let the baby stay. Rebecca complains to Aunt Jane about the disappointment, and Aunt Jane answers that no printed book could cover all the things Rebecca wants to do. The excerpt ends with Rebecca dressing the baby in the bureau area, pinning her red flannel petticoat. A single out-of-place sentence about Diana viewing a painting in 2013 appears mid-passage and is unrelated to the story.
one_line: A fiction excerpt in which Rebecca tries to keep a borrowed baby for Sunday, is refused by Miss Miranda, and turns to Aunt Jane for comfort.
key_facts: Rebecca brought the Simpson baby home from the farm, hoping it would help the household get through a dull Sunday.
Miss Miranda refuses to let the borrowed baby stay and tells Rebecca to give the child supper and carry her home.
Mrs. Simpson had been planning to go to Milltown, and Rebecca says she will be dreadfully disappointed.
Emma Jane has the promise of the baby's next Sunday and Alice Robinson has the promise of the one after that.
Mrs. Simpson wanted Rebecca to have the baby first because Rebecca had so much experience with babies.
Mrs. Simpson says the baby, who has yellow hair and big blue eyes, takes after her father.
Miss Miranda says the baby could not take after her father because he would take anything there was before she got there.
Aunt Jane was sorting clean sheets and pillow cases for Saturday in the linen closet upstairs when Rebecca sought her out.
Rebecca describes the baby as the fat, gurgly kind, not thin and fussy like some babies.
Rebecca says she wishes she had a printed book listing everything she could do so she would not be disappointed so often.
Aunt Jane replies that no printed book could fit Rebecca because nobody could imagine beforehand the things she would want to do.
Rebecca plans to drag the baby home in the little soap-wagon.
Rebecca turns the baby upside down, removes a crooked pin from her waistband, and attaches her red flannel petticoat with a large safety pin at the bureau.
An inserted sentence states that in 2013, after waiting in line for hours, Diana finally saw the original 'Impression, Sunrise' painting up close, which breaks from the narrative.
